summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and epigastric pain. She developed early signs of diabetic ketoacidosis with a falling bicarbonate and rising anion gap, which resolved with IV fluids and insulin adjustment. Despite improvement in metabolic parameters, nausea persisted, and she was diagnosed with viral gastroenteritis. She tolerated a gradual return to oral intake and was stabilized on insulin with a temporary reduction in Lantus due to hypoglycemia. Chronic low back pain was evaluated with a normal lumbar spine X-ray; treatment shifted to non-narcotic methods including acetaminophen and lidocaine patches. She was discharged home in stable condition with new prescriptions for compazine and ranitidine, clear insulin instructions, and follow-up plans.
